markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize **terminal-focused BERT4Rec training with multiple uniform negatives**: a small, testable change addressing current-intent mismatch and weak discrimination.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Random reconstruction differs from next-item prediction. Terminal masking directly matches appended-mask inference. (2) Industrial and Electronics show 12.25% and 11.27% wrong-rank rates. Their negative lower-tail margins motivate stronger discrimination. (3) Users report stale interests and broadly plausible alternatives displacing specific choices. These observations motivate recent-prefix supervision, but do not establish compatibility labels.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) includes final-item masking. Increasing its training share preserves the family. (2) [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates emphasizing recent targets under limited computation. It did not evaluate BERT4Rec, so transfer remains hypothetical. (3) [Correcting LogQ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) distinguishes always-included positives from sampled negatives. Sampling corrections reduce bias; they do not identify false negatives.

**Framework.** Three directions separate the problem: target alignment changes which hidden item is predicted; discrimination changes competing items; feature specificity changes available representations. Terminal training occupies the first direction, multiple negatives the second, and scratch-trained title features the third. None supplies observed ownership, compatibility, or mood.

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are 0–10; difficulty increases with implementation cost. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Recent-prefix terminal ranking, multiple uniform negatives | 3: useful combination; established parts | 8: transferable; unverified | 8: recent priorities and competing broad matches; compatibility unknown | 8: targets weak margins; generalization uncertain | 3: local changes; sampling care |
| B. Corrected stochastic hard-negative objective | 5: careful combination; known methods | 7: efficient discrimination; false negatives | 6: specific competitors; no recency mechanism | 8: hard cases; biased selection risk | 6: tractable; proposal accounting |
| C. Joint ID/title encoder trained from scratch | 5: constrained adaptation; established fusion | 7: fine details; sparse text learning | 8: identifiers and purpose; mood ambiguous | 6: differentiated items; margins unproven | 7: one network; tokenization overhead |

**Selected algorithm: A.** Sample training-only prefixes, favoring recent endpoints while retaining uniform coverage. Replace each endpoint target with the reserved mask and remove its entire suffix. Optimize masked-target discrimination against multiple uniformly sampled unseen training items. This addresses two reported failures: outdated priorities receive less supervision, while competing plausible items face a stronger ranking objective. Improved specificity remains a hypothesis, particularly for incompatibility and duplication.

```
endpoint ~ mixture(uniform, recent)
input = left_pad(history[:endpoint] + [MASK])
h = BERT(input)[final_nonpadding_position]
loss = mean(softplus(score(h, negatives) - score(h, target)))
```

Exclude all known training positives from negatives. Start with 50% terminal examples and 32 negatives; retain baseline random masking otherwise. Preserve one checkpoint/category, routing, seeds, limits, predictor consistency, and diagnostic interfaces. Select only by fixed macro validation HR@10; check lower-tail margins without treating them as generalization evidence.

idea.description: Increase terminal-mask supervision within the corrected BERT4Rec and use multiple uniform negatives for each hidden target. Train exactly one model per category, preserving the bidirectional masked-item backbone and appended-mask inference.
idea.motivation: Recent-prefix terminal supervision explicitly addresses historical interests outweighing present priorities. Multiple competing negatives address broadly plausible items displacing stronger specific matches. The measured negative 10th-percentile margins in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics provide a model-facing reason to test stronger discrimination. Compatibility, ownership, duplication, and mood remain unobserved; improvements on those behaviors cannot be assumed.
idea.implementation_notes: Modify the supplied baseline rather than reconstructing its unavailable implementation. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four routes, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. For terminal examples, sample an endpoint t>=1 from training histories, use only history[:t] as context, and replace history[t] with the reserved mask. Mix uniform endpoint sampling with exponentially recent endpoint sampling; initialize mixture weights at 0.5 and recency half-life at 10 interactions as experimental settings. Allocate 50% of examples to terminal masking and retain baseline masked-target examples otherwise. Use 32 uniformly sampled negatives excluding the user's known training positives; reduce the count when the eligible pool is smaller. Average pairwise logistic loss across negatives and masked targets so additional negatives do not simply multiply gradient scale. This is a pairwise objective, not a claimed unbiased softmax estimator; no logQ correction is required. Compare against the baseline using the host's fixed macro validation HR@10. Inference remains the single trained BERT4Rec with an appended mask and final nonpadding readout. Update the embedded predictor writer if any model signature or configuration changes. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and ModelView compatibility. Diagnostic margins must use hidden targets and training-only inputs; report the masking and negative-sampling protocol, since changing it affects comparability. Do not interpret missing category metadata or unidentified simulator items as negative preference evidence.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    initialize corrected BERT4Rec using training seed 42
    for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
        for batch in range(200):
            examples = []
            for sampled training history H:
                if terminal_branch(probability=0.5):
                    t = sample_endpoint(H, uniform_recent_mixture=0.5)
                    sequence = left_pad(truncate_context(H[:t]) + [MASK])
                    supervised_positions = [final_nonpadding_position(sequence)]
                    targets = [H[t]]
                else:
                    sequence, supervised_positions, targets = baseline_masked_example(H)
                negatives = uniform_items_excluding_training_positives(H, count=32)
                features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                positive_scores = model.predict_score(features[supervised_positions], targets)
                negative_scores = model.predict_score(features[supervised_positions], negatives)
                examples.append(mean(softplus(negative_scores - positive_scores)))
            optimize(mean(examples))
    save exactly one selected model checkpoint and its configuration
    emit predictor using the same architecture and appended-mask readout
select proposal using host macro validation HR@10 only

originality.positive: Combines endpoint sampling and multiple-negative discrimination in a minimal BERT4Rec experiment tied to the supplied diagnoses.
originality.negative: Terminal masking, recency sampling, and pairwise logistic ranking are established techniques; the contribution is their constrained application.

future_potential.positive: A successful result would justify systematic study of training-target alignment under fixed recommendation compute budgets.
future_potential.negative: No supplied validation evidence establishes gains, and recent endpoint emphasis may weaken long-term preference coverage.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires sampler and loss changes while retaining the baseline backbone, scoring interface, and predictor architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct suffix removal, target hiding, padding readout, and eligible-negative sampling require careful implementation.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Includes final-item masking to support next-item prediction.
limitations: Does not establish the best terminal-example proportion for this benchmark.
Random reconstruction can provide context unavailable at next-item inference.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates recent-target sampling for efficient sequential recommendation training.
limitations: Does not evaluate BERT4Rec, so applying its sampling principle here is an experimental adaptation.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Distinguishes always-included positives from sampled negatives in sampled-softmax correction.
limitations: Sampling correction does not detect false negatives.
Its softmax correction is not required by the selected pairwise logistic objective.

related_work.title: Sampled Estimators For Softmax Must Be Biased
contributions: Establishes limitations of subset-only softmax estimators.
limitations: Does not establish recommendation gains for a particular sampling strategy or pairwise objective.
